CausalChain: Epigenetic modifications and dysregulated transcription factors -> Altered alternative splicing of the CLDN18 gene -> Upregulation and selective expression of CLDN18.2 in tumor cells -> Exposure to immunosuppressive signals and cytokines in the tumor microenvironment -> Modulation of CLDN18.2 therapy efficacy and emergence of resistance -> Potential improvement through combination strategies
Hypothesis: Modulation of epigenetic regulators and tumor microenvironmental factors governs the cancer-specific expression and therapeutic responsiveness of CLDN18.2; therefore, concurrently targeting these regulatory mechanisms along with CLDN18.2 could overcome resistance and synergistically enhance anti-tumor efficacy in solid tumors.
Abstract: Emerging research on CLDN18.2‐targeted therapies in various solid tumors, particularly gastric cancer, has revealed promising clinical effects, yet several key mechanistic and translational questions remain unanswered. In particular, the precise molecular controls over alternative splicing yielding the cancer‐selective CLDN18.2 isoform, the influence of the tumor microenvironment on its expression and on treatment responsiveness, and the optimal strategies to combine CLDN18.2 targeting with other modalities such as immune checkpoint inhibitors or antiangiogenic agents are not fully understood. Addressing these gaps could refine patient selection and pave the way for improved combinatorial therapies. Here, we propose that dissecting the interplay between epigenetic modifications, transcriptional regulation, and extrinsic signals from the tumor microenvironment will be fundamental to overcoming resistance and enhancing the efficacy of CLDN18.2‐targeted treatments.
